content.title: Oscillate Wildly: Delaware’s Borrowed Corporate Law and an Unstable SEC
content.abstract: U.S. corporate law has two main sources. Delaware and other states govern the corporation's internal affairs, especially fiduciary duties, while federal law governs disclosure, including in mergers and tender offers. The two are intertwined: important Delaware doctrines, such as Revlon, Corwin, and C & J Energy, and the safe harbors of SB 21 rely on federal inputs, from disclosure rules to the minimum tender offer period and exchange listing standards.
